must_fix.issue: Save-the-date and invitation timing is vague under a heading that promises it: 'send them earlier than you would for a local one' (r2 line 70) and 'early enough that guests can still book flights and leave' (r2 line 129). Primary persona's medium issue, raised by 3 personas.
must_fix.fix: Give practical timing as advice, not as a fact or statistic: e.g. for a destination wedding, send save-the-dates as soon as the date and venue are confirmed, ideally around 9 to 12 months out; send invitations with travel details around 3 to 4 months out, earlier if guests need visas or long-haul leave, with the RSVP date set before final numbers are due. Phrase as 'we suggest' guidance. No averages, surveys or percentages. Update the at-a-glance table rows to match.

must_fix.issue: First screen does not answer the search: Key takeaways lead with Australian legal admin (NOIM, passports) and the at-a-glance table sits near the bottom (r2 line 235), after the destination explainer. Secondary persona's core complaint; the table is the most-shared element (planner_couple, sceptic, search_visitor).
must_fix.fix: Rewrite Key takeaways to lead with the countdown (12 months: budget, guests, style, venue; 10 to 11: key suppliers and save-the-dates; 6 to 7: passports, rings, stationery; 4 to 5: invitations; final month: legal and supplier check), then one takeaway for the legal and passport points labelled 'if marrying in Australia' or 'travelling on an Australian passport'. Move the recap table (or a short version) up to sit straight after Key takeaways; keep the full table at the end if useful. No new facts.

must_fix.issue: First Concierge pitch sits in the destination intro before any checklist evidence, and 'plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world' raises the commission and accountability question unanswered (r2 line 27).
must_fix.fix: Remove the line-27 Concierge sentence (keep the destination checklist link). The first Concierge mention is the primary CTA after the 8 to 9 months section, per brief. Lead with the specific brand-facts claims (one Wedded Advisor, works in your time zone, fee agreed in writing before any work begins, suppliers paid at standardised industry rates). No fee amount, fee basis or commission figures. Keep UTMs.

must_fix.issue: Money and accountability gap: the only contract line is 'Pay outstanding balances on the dates in each contract' (1 month out). Nothing on deposits, cancellation, or room-block shortfall paid to overseas suppliers months earlier.
must_fix.fix: Add questions to ask, not promises: at 10 to 11 months, when booking the venue and suppliers, get the deposit amount, payment schedule, cancellation and postponement terms in writing, and ask what happens to deposits if a supplier cancels; for the room block, ask who is liable for unfilled rooms after the release date. Point to declaring and checking cover with the travel insurer. No deposit protection claims, no statement of who holds contracts.

must_fix.issue: No accessibility task for older or less mobile guests anywhere in the year.
must_fix.fix: Add to the destination track (site visit and week of): ask the venue about a step-free route from arrival to ceremony and reception, seating and shade for older guests, and accessible transfers and rooms. Questions only.

must_fix.issue: Large or high-profile weddings get nothing: room block only, and a public wedding website with no privacy note (r2 line 66).
must_fix.fix: Add one destination-track line: for a large guest list, ask whether exclusive use of the whole property is possible instead of a room block. Beside the website advice: keep guest details private or password protected, and ask suppliers about confidentiality and social posting. Questions only, no brand claims about scale or security.

should_fix.fix: Add a few words from brand-facts.md: Wonderland Studio, our planning app for RSVPs and seating charts. No price or 'free' claim.
